advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider forcing `frontier` in review_ticket(): either revert to raw cfg.model (register as _CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN like spec_scan) or scope the class binding to the actual reviewer, and reconcile the treatment with the identical spec_scan site.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/operations.py:152: `cfg = replace(cfg, model=resolve_model_string(FRONTIER_CLASS))` — applied unconditionally, before `rid = reviewer_id or default_reviewer_id()` at line 155, so it precedes and ignores reviewer selection

The ticket's own final author comment (rebar afeb-bc04-3265-4747) recommends reverting this exact site: "review_ticket ... is a top-level op's primary call — cfg.model IS the knob ... an operator who steers by setting the bare llm.model CONFIG-FILE key no longer steers rebar review at all — it is pinned to whatever frontier resolves to (opus by default)"

This is structurally identical to spec_scan._scan_epics_inner, which the same change registered as `_CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN` (a top-level op's primary call) rather than binding a class — the two sites are treated inconsistently
advisory.finding: review_ticket() now forces the `frontier` model class for EVERY reviewer_id, overriding the operator's cfg.model for a single-call top-level op. The justification comment only reasons about the default `ticket-quality` reviewer, but the op accepts arbitrary reviewer_id (e.g. `completion-verifier`, a verification-style reviewer) which is likewise pinned to frontier; and it removes the operator's single-knob (config-file `llm.model`) control over `rebar review`, hardcoding a class for config-file users.

operations.py runs inside `gate_source.gate_read_root(handle)` with `cfg = gate_source.apply_handle(cfg, handle)` (operations.py:136-138), so the pinned snapshot root that from_env honoured is not honoured by the unqualified class-table read
dropped.finding: The four new `resolve_model_string(CLASS)` calls omit the `repo_root` argument, so `load_class_slots()` reads the `[tool.rebar.llm.model_classes]` table from the default/CWD repo root rather than the config's `cfg.repo_path`. In review_ticket this runs under a pinned gate code root (gate_read_root/apply_handle set cfg.repo_path), and enrich() takes an explicit repo_root — so the class table may be read from a different root than the rest of the config, unlike the established batch-runner pattern which passes repo_root.
